p: Jesus was born in Bethlehem of: Christ a poor child, laid down in a crib, and though given no attention by his own people, receives nonetheless a noble witness of his divinity from heaven, and of his kingly estate from strangers: which his own people unknowingly let happen, although they did not acknowledge him.
Judaea in the days of Herod: For there was another in the tribe of Zebulun.
wise men from the east to: Wise and learned men: It is a Persian word which they use frequently.
troubled: Was much moved, for he was a foreigner, and became ruler by force; and the Jews were troubled; for wickedness is mad and raging.
chief priests and: The chief priests, that is, such as were of Aaron's family, who were divided into twenty-four orders. 1Ch 24:5; 2Ch 36:14.
scribes of the people together: They that expound the law to the people, for the Hebrews take this word for another, which means as much as to expound and to declare.
least among the princes of Juda: Though you are a small town, yet you will be very famous and notable through the birth of the Messiah, who will be born in you.
shall rule my people Israel: That will rule and govern: for kings are rightly called leaders and shepherds of the people.
fell down: A kind of humble and lovely reverence.
treasures: The rich and costly presents, which they brought him.
warned of God in a dream: God warned and told them of it, even though they did not ask him.
And when they were departed: Christ having just been born, begins to be crucified for us, both in himself, and also in his members.
by Jeremy the prophet: For God speaketh by the mouth of the prophets.
a voice heard: A voice of lamenting, weeping and howling.

Rachel weeping for her children: That is to say, All who live around Bethlehem: for Rachel, Jacob's wife who died in childbirth, was buried by the road that leads to this town, which is also called Ephratah, because of the fruitfulness of the soil, and the plentifulness of corn.

But when Herod was dead: Christ is brought up in Nazareth, after the death of the tyrant by God's providence: that by the very name of the place it might plainly appear to the world that he is the Lord's true Nazarite.
